To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proton T(2) and T(1)-relaxation rates are well described by the stochastic Liouille approach (SLA) with a single process dynamic model.
the proton T(2)-NMRD and T(1)-T(2)-ratio data of Gd(H2O)(8)(+) are well reproduced by both the stochastic Liouvile approach (SLA) and the generalized Solomon-Blogembergen-Morgan theory (GSBM).

the analysis of T(1)- NMRD profiles of a solution of Gd(H2O)8(3+), recorded at different glycerol concentrations, at different temperatures and at different magnetic fields, do not result in an unambiguous description of the electron and nuclear spin system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the proton T-1 NMRD profiles of paramagnetic ions in solution.
the question whether proton NMRD profiles of paramagnetic metal ions in solution can be used for a reliable description of the electron-spin system.
the question: can we determine the microscopic parameters of a paramagnetic ion from the analysis of the water proton T(1) relaxation rate?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proton T(2)-NMRD analysis of the Gd(DOTA)(-) complex is not conclusive with respect to the microscopic parameters of the electron spin relaxation mechanism, and that the proton T-1 NMRD analysis of Gd(H2O)(8)(+) is also not conclusive with respect the microscopic parameters of electron spin relaxation mechanism.
the proton T(2)-NMRD analysis of Gd(H2O)(8)(+) is not a sufficient basis to draw a reliable picture of the microscopic properties of the electron spin systems of this complex.
both models, the GSBM and SLA, are equally valid, but that the SLA is more appropriate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
proton T(1) relaxation data are not sufficient to fully determine the microscopic parameters for the electron spin system of the Gd(3+)-ion.

the analysis of the proton T-1-NMRD profiles of paramagnetic ions in solution is a useful tool to obtain microscopic information about the electronic spin system of the paramagnetic ion, but the analysis should be complemented with other experimental techniques.
the proton T(2) and T(1) relaxation data are consistent with a model in which the ZFS is modulated by the reorientation of the water molecules in the first coordination sphere of the Gd(3+) ion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis of T(1) relaxation rates of water protons of a paramagnetic ion is not necessarily a good probe of its microscopic properties.
it is necessary to perform a ESR lineshape study in order to obtain reliable microscopic parameters from the analysis of the proton T1-NMRD profile of Gd(H2O)8(3+) complex.

proton T(1) relaxation data are sensitive to the dynamic model of the correlation function of the ZFS, whereas the ESR lineshape data are sensitive to both the dynamic and the static part of the model.
